payload.instruction: transform the black DVD into a white DVD
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Was the specific black DVD in the source image transformed so that the same DVD is visibly white in the edited image?
node.criteria: Pass only if the source DVD can be confidently matched to an object in the edited image and that same object is visibly white rather than black; fail if the matched DVD remains black or the source DVD is absent without being transformed; unknown if the source DVD's identity or correspondence cannot be determined.
node.binding: Compare the source and edited images, tracking the requested black DVD by its visible shape, location, and surrounding scene context. Do not treat a newly appearing white disc as evidence that the source DVD was recolored; report unknown when correspondence is ambiguous.

node_traces.evidence: The source DVD appears as a small rectangular case or disc-like object near the center of the snow. In the edited image, two white circular discs are visible, but neither can be confidently matched to that source object by shape and scene context; the source object’s correspondence is ambiguous.

d2: The binding over-focuses on whether the source item is independently recognizable as a DVD and explicitly directs uncertainty when identity is not confident. In the images, the small rectangular item near the center is replaced by a white disc at roughly the same location, while another white disc is on the dark object to the right; the source item’s DVD identity and which edited disc corresponds to it are not established. This is genuine visual ambiguity, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure. Keep the identity/correspondence check, but make its evidence procedure distinguish the candidate discs using location, shape, and scene context, and separate “the requested edit visibly progressed” from “the same source object remains identifiable as a DVD.” The rubric’s aggregate label is no, but it is not atomic ground truth for this identity criterion; do not force a fail or infer that no edit occurred from the unresolved trace. The high-confidence unknown and zero coverage indicate the criterion/binding may be routing an aggregate progress judgment through an identity-only check. Clarify that this node should return only the identity judgment, leaving requested-change progress to the appropriate criterion, and reserve unknown for cases where correspondence or identity truly cannot be resolved.

response.content: {"text":"The binding already asks for source-to-edited correspondence, but its instruction to report unknown whenever correspondence is ambiguous may make the node stop at uncertainty instead of evaluating the visible evidence. Keep the identity check, and direct the node to compare the source item’s position and surrounding scene with each edited candidate, weighing location alongside shape and context rather than requiring the DVD to remain independently recognizable. Here, the source shows a small rectangular item near the center; the edit shows a white disc near that location and another on the dark object to the right. The trace should assess these candidates explicitly, without assuming either is the same DVD or treating a new white disc as proof of recoloring. Keep identity/correspondence separate from whether any requested change visibly progressed, so this node returns only its identity judgment and the aggregate criterion can assess progress elsewhere. Reserve unknown for genuinely unresolved correspondence; do not force a fail from the aggregate “no” label. This is a semantic/routing issue, not a transport, schema, or dependency failure."}
